title: Does a residual audio-sync error show at the cuts of an automatic multi-camera edit?
summary: Edit quality cannot show it (a camera is shifted in score and picture together), so this counts continuity at each cut: the jump in world time between the two cameras, and loud events inside it. 4 cameras, a 120 s Viterbi edit from capture-edit at a random point of a 1 h shoot, camera clocks uniform in ±40 ppm, sync errors from the real capture-audiosync GCC-PHAT estimator on synthetic audio (12 seeds). A sync made once and never redone leaves 50% of cuts jumping over one 30 fps frame (mean jump 40 ms); a Theil–Sen fit over 12 windows leaves none from 0 dB down to −10 dB SNR with 2 s windows (−15 dB with 5 s). Below that it flips to 69–98% of cuts jumping 0.3–0.5 s with 11–24% of cuts repeating or dropping a loud event. A threshold, not a slope. Synthetic audio, assumed event rate 0.5/s and one-frame visibility criterion; ppm range swept, not sourced; no real footage and no viewer test.
lede: does a residual audio-sync error show at the cuts of an automatic edit? A sync made once leaves 50% of cuts jumping over a frame; a robust fit leaves none down to -10 dB SNR (2 s windows) and then fails outright, with 11 to 24% of cuts repeating or dropping a loud event.
